messages:
hao: quick dump from this morning's perf sweep + question about per-GPU token budgets. ran model-x on A10/T4/L4/A100/H100 with continuous batching tweaks. noticed weird non-linear throughput when batch token total > ~30k on T4. attaching short config and numbers below.

sam: can you paste the exact configs and the profile output? was this with the new kernel-selector flags?

hao: yeah, kernel_selector=auto, use_mixed_precision=true, kv_cache_prefetch=on. core config we used:

```
continuous_batching: {
  max_batch_size: 64
  max_tokens_per_batch: 50000  # global starting point
  queue_policy: "latency_slo"  # try latency-first
  token_budget_per_gpu: {
    A100: 100000,
    H100: 150000,
    A10: 30000,
    L4: 40000,
    T4: 15000
  }
}
```

hao: profile highlights: T4 40k tokens batch -> 18% lower throughput than predicted; A10 degrades ~10% past 28k; L4 behaves like A10 but slightly better; A100/H100 scale linearly up to our max test (~120k) then memory pressure spikes. KV hit rate ~22% for long contexts which helped A100 but not T4.

maria: are you grouping by seq_len when forming batches? mixed seqs can blow up token count quickly.

hao: yes we did dynamic packing by seq_len buckets (0-128,129-512,512+). still saw the T4 cliff inside 129-512 bucket when we accumulate many 512s.

jess: that sounds like kernel selection fallback to slower kernels at certain sequence shapes. did the logs show any kernel warnings?

hao: good call — kernel_selector logged fallbacks on T4: switched from fused_attention to generic_attention for seq>384 in a few instances. attaches snippet of selector log.

ops-bot: [deploy] canary rollout of runtime v2.14 started by @dinesh 2026-01-07T09:05:21Z

sam: if kernel_selector is toggling to generic kernels, our perf model needs to penalize those shapes more. maybe set per-gpu token thresholds to avoid hitting the fallback. e.g., on T4 keep max_tokens_per_batch <= 12k for 512-token requests mixed in.

maria: another lever — KV cache prefetch behavior: if many requests reuse prefixes, we should prefer packing same-prefix requests into the same batch to avoid duplicating KV mem usage. that helps A10/L4.

dinesh: spotted a regression after yesterday's quantization change: T4 median latency up 8% for 1-2k token requests when batching enabled. suspect kernel microcode selection plus lower occupancy. rolling back quant change removed regression.

hao: action items I'm proposing:
- set conservative GPU-specific defaults for max_tokens_per_batch: T4=12000, A10=28000, L4=32000, A100=110000, H100=140000
- reduce max_batch_size for T4 to 32 when avg seq_len>256
- add kernel-selector telemetry to per-route dashboards (owner: sam)
- experiment with "same-prefix packing" to improve KV reuse (owner: maria)
- re-run quantization tests with kernel pinning to validate regressions (owner: dinesh)

jess: +1. also suggest adding a safety circuit: if kernel_selector logs >5 fallbacks in 1min on a GPU, throttle token_budget for that GPU down 20% for 2m automatically. could avoid large cliffs.

sam: seems reasonable. also let's log per-batch: gpu_type, total_tokens, max_seq_len, selected_kernel, kv_hit_rate. that'll help feed the auto-tuning loop.

maria: will prototype same-prefix packing in the local harness. should be able to A/B with & without KV reuse.

dinesh: I'll reproduce the quant regression with explicit kernel pinning and capture perf counters (smem, l2, warp occupancy). if it's microcode or kernel change, we can patch kernel_selector rules.

hao: cool. plan to push conservative per-gpu defaults to staging and run 24h soak. i'll post a short dashboard link when it's up. any other concerns?

sam: one more — document these thresholds in README and expose as suggested presets in the Console UI so customers on T4 see a warning when they set permissive budgets.

jess: also add an automated perf test targeting extreme shapes (lots of 512s) that'll run daily against each GPU type.

hao: noted. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

maria: ping me after the soak so I can grab KV hit traces for the same-prefix experiments.

ops-bot: [ci] perf-tests/continuous-batching started by jess (job 8721)

hao: marked owners and will follow up in #eng-runtime in ~24h with results.
